name: Spodumene
physical: Said to bring a calm, unhurried feeling
Crystal healers link it with relief from stress-related tension
summary: Spodumene is the lithium pyroxene behind kunzite and hiddenite, a calm, pale stone in crystal lore linked with peace, balance and gentle clarity.
intro: Spodumene is a lithium aluminium silicate that forms long, flat, ridged crystals and sometimes gives the world its largest gem crystals: giants of more than fourteen metres have been found in South Dakota's Etta Mine. Plain spodumene is grey, white, yellow or colourless, and is sometimes called triphane. Its two famous coloured varieties are pink kunzite and green hiddenite, but the plain stone has its own quiet appeal, a soft pearly glow along its cleavage faces. Beyond gems, spodumene is the most important hard-rock source of lithium, so it is central to modern battery technology.
history: The name spodumene comes from the Greek spodumenos, meaning burnt to ashes, referring to the ash-grey colour it turns when heated in a blowpipe. It was first described in 1800 by the Brazilian scientist Jose Bonifacio de Andrada e Silva, who found it in Sweden's Utö mine. Lithium was first isolated from it in the early nineteenth century. In 1879 and 1902 the coloured varieties hiddenite and kunzite were discovered in North Carolina and California respectively. Giant crystals from the Black Hills of South Dakota became famous in the twentieth century. Today Australia leads global lithium production from spodumene.
meaning: In the crystal tradition spodumene is a calming, balancing stone. Because it contains lithium, a mineral long associated with emotional steadiness in folk belief, practitioners connect it with peace of mind and mild emotional balance, although it is used purely as a symbolic aid. It is said to settle nerves, help with a clear head and bring gentleness to a busy mind. Plain spodumene is linked to the heart and crown chakras and used in meditation for quiet insight. Many people prefer it as a subtle stone that does not overwhelm. Physically it is traditionally associated with relaxation and a calm, unhurried feeling, as a comfort stone only and never a replacement for care.
howToUse: Hold a piece of spodumene during meditation or before sleep, breathing slowly and letting your thoughts settle. Place a crystal on your desk if your work environment is stressful, or keep a small stone in your pocket. In a grid, it pairs with selenite and clear quartz to create an atmosphere of calm. Wear a spodumene piece as a pendant if you want a quiet reminder to pause. If you also own kunzite or hiddenite, keep them together as a spodumene trio.
care: Spodumene has perfect cleavage and can be brittle, so protect it from knocks. Clean it with lukewarm water and a soft cloth, avoiding ultrasonic and steam cleaners. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or selenite. Strong sunlight can fade some coloured spodumene, so store it in a shaded place. Wrap raw crystals individually in soft cloth, since the blade-like terminations and thin edges can chip easily.
identify: Spodumene is recognisable by its flat, vertically striated crystals, perfect cleavage and pearly to glassy sheen. Look-alikes include quartz, feldspar, tremolite, kyanite and clear topaz. It is heavier than quartz and shows two distinct cleavage directions at nearly right angles. Gem material is sometimes irradiated or heated. For jewelry-grade pieces, ask a seller to identify any treatment. Spodumene sold as a lithium ore sample is a safe, natural mineral specimen, but should still be handled with ordinary care.

faq.a: Spodumene is a lithium aluminium silicate mineral in the pyroxene group. It occurs in grey, white and yellow forms, and its coloured gem varieties include pink kunzite and green hiddenite.

faq.q: What is spodumene used for in crystal work?
faq.a: Practitioners use it for calm, balance and quiet meditation. Because it contains lithium, it is symbolically associated with emotional steadiness, and it is kept as a gentle, soothing companion.
Plain spodumene crystals are inexpensive collectables, while gem-quality kunzite and hiddenite are worth more. Industrially, spodumene is a major source of lithium used in batteries.
